newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments up on last year.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments up on last year.

text.p: Latest European Union figures show grain export commitments between July 1 and November 19 were 4.6 percent above their year-ago level, mostly the result of higher flour and barley sales, member-country officials said on Monday.
The figures, based on delivered export certificates, showed grain exports ahead on last year at 11.578 million tonnes against 11.069 million.
Flour export commitments reached 2.815 million tonnes up from 2.734 million during the same period last year.
Last week the EU cleared bids by European flour firms to export around 500,000 tonnes of soft wheat flour under licences carrying a daily refund of 27 Ecus per tonne.
Commercial barley exports jumped to 2.416 million tonnes from 984,000 tonnes during the same period last year, helped by sales to Saudi Arabia.
Commercial wheat exports however were still lagging on last year at 3.313 million tonnes against 3.756 million.
Malt exports fell to 1.749 million tonnes from 1.908 million tonnes.
Commercial oat commitments reached 183,000 tonnes. The EU made no oat sales during the same period last year.
Since November 19, the EU has granted 311,300 tonnes of soft wheat, 268,000 tonnes of barley, 43,597 tonnes of rye and 1,500 tonnes of oats exports through its weekly grain tender system.
